import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-! # Hartshorne's conjecture on Vector Bundles

*References:*
* [Har1974] R. Hartshorne, [Varieties of small codimension in projective space](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society-new-series/volume-80/issue-6/Varieties-of-small-codimension-in-projective-space/bams/1183535999.full).
* [MO2010] [Evidences on Hartshorne's conjecture? References?](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/13990/evidences-on-hartshornes-conjecture-references)
-/

open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial AlgebraicGeometry

universe u
variable (S : Scheme.{u})

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

/--
A vector bundle over a scheme `S` is a locally free $\mathcal{O}_S$-module of finite rank.
-/
structure VectorBundles where
  carrier : S.Modules
  rank : ℕ
  isLocallyFreeFiniteConstantRank : SheafOfModules.IsVectorBundleWithRank
    (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology S) carrier rank

instance (S : Scheme) : Coe S.VectorBundles S.Modules where
  coe 𝓕 := 𝓕.carrier

/--
Vector bundles form a category.
-/
instance : Category S.VectorBundles :=
  inferInstanceAs <| Category <| InducedCategory _ VectorBundles.carrier

def VectorBundles.toModule : S.VectorBundles ⥤ S.Modules where
  obj 𝓕 := 𝓕.carrier
  map f := f.hom

@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem hasFiniteCoproductsVectorBundles : HasFiniteCoproducts S.VectorBundles := by
  sorry

instance : HasFiniteCoproducts S.VectorBundles :=
  hasFiniteCoproductsVectorBundles S

variable {S} in
/--
A splitting of a vector bundle `𝓕` is a non-trivial direct sum decomposition of `𝓕`
-/
structure VectorBundles.Splitting (𝓕 : S.VectorBundles) (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] where
  components : ι → S.VectorBundles
  iso : 𝓕 ≅ ∐ components
  non_trivial : ∀ i, IsEmpty (components i ≅ 𝓕)

instance {S : Scheme} (𝓕 : S.VectorBundles) (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] :
    CoeOut (𝓕.Splitting ι) (ι → S.VectorBundles) where
  coe s := s.components

-- TODO(lezeau): here we would really need some sanity checks and easier results.

/--
There are no indecomposable vector bundles of rank 2 on $\mathbb{P}^n$ for $n \ge 7$.
This is Conjecture 6.3 in [Har1974].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 14]
theorem harthshorne_conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 7 ≤ n)
    (𝓕 : VectorBundles ℙ(Fin (n + 1); Spec (.of ℂ)))
    (h𝓕 : 𝓕.rank = 2) :
    Nonempty (𝓕.Splitting (Fin 2)) := by
  sorry

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

reformulations.difference: Rather than explicitly requiring two line bundles, the conclusion requests a Fin 2-indexed categorical coproduct decomposition into constant finite-rank locally free sheaves, with neither summand isomorphic to the original bundle.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On nonempty, connected projective space over ℂ, locally free finite-rank sheaves are algebraic vector bundles with constant rank. The induced category has exactly the underlying module-sheaf morphisms, and its finite coproducts correspond to ordinary direct sums. If either of the two summands were zero, the other would be isomorphic to the whole, contradicting non_trivial. Their positive ranks add to 2, so both have rank 1. Conversely, a direct sum of two line bundles supplies the required splitting, since rank invariance prevents either line bundle from being isomorphic to a rank-two bundle. Thus this is precisely the asserted absence of indecomposable rank-two bundles. The categorical/direct-sum equivalence and exclusion of zero summands were proved in scratch Lean; the complete equivalence including the rank argument was checked mathematically, not fully formalized.

sources_consulted: R. Hartshorne, “Varieties of small codimension in projective space,” Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 80 (1974), 1017–1032: introduction and §6, especially Conjecture 6.3 and the definition of indecomposable on p. 1028. AMS copy: https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1974-80-06/S0002-9904-1974-13612-8/S0002-9904-1974-13612-8.pdf (read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1974-80-06/S0002-9904-1974-13612-8/S0002-9904-1974-13612-8.pdf).
https://mathoverflow.net/questions/12688/nonsingular-normal-schemes/12689#12689 — linked discussion of the complex-projective formulation and the bound n ≥ 7.
https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.2763 — abstract and version-history remarks concerning the restricted quadratic-equation case.

Local definitions in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/VectorBundle.lean and FormalConjecturesForMathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpace.lean, together with the underlying Mathlib definitions of scheme modules, free and restricted sheaves, covering families, induced categories, and finite coproducts.
review.notes: All declarations were checked, including the finite-coproduct API and coercions. Finite direct sums preserve local freeness and constant finite rank, so the API statement is mathematically valid. The projective-space construction has n+1 homogeneous coordinates and the correct complex base. Scratch files /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/checks.lean compile successfully. Tests establish that empty covers cannot trivialize local freeness on a nonempty base, singleton splittings are impossible, binary splittings exclude zero summands, and rank-two bundles satisfying the hypotheses exist; the latter construction uses no sorry axioms. No answer slots, formal-proof claims, or status discrepancies were found.
